name: Flower Mart
acresNote: The Development Agreement (Planning Commission packet for July 18, 2019, case 2017-000663) and the Oct 1, 2026 Planning Commission agenda: the approximately 6.5-acre Flower Mart site, Assessor's Block 3778, Lots 001B, 002B, 004, 005, 047 and 048. The parcels drawn come to about 6.8 acres.

program.notes: Approved in 2019 (Motion 20484): three office buildings of 8 to 18 stories, up to about 236 ft, with 2,032,165 sq ft of office, a new wholesale flower market of 113,036 sq ft, 83,459 sq ft of retail and 35,450 sq ft of public open space, built in three phases; a variant without the flower market had 2,061,380 sq ft of office, 90,976 sq ft of retail, a 22,690 sq ft child care center and a 950 sq ft community room. No homes. Under the 2019 Development Agreement the developer builds a new flower market on the site or pays for one elsewhere in San Francisco, moves the vendors to an interim site at 2000 Marin Street, dedicates a site of at least 14,000 sq ft for affordable housing and gives $5 million to the Sunnydale Hub project. Proposed (2025-26): an amended Development Agreement, a new Flower Mart Special Use District and height limits raised from 160 and 270 ft to between 350 and 600 ft; depending on the scenario the project could include up to 3,532 homes with office, retail and cultural, institutional and educational uses (Oct 1, 2026 agenda). The 2025 application describes a base scheme of five buildings up to 270 ft with 2,660,700 sq ft of office/lab, and residential (about 3,500 homes), mixed-use (about 1,242 homes and 1,493,600 sq ft of office/lab) and institutional variants.

publicPartners: San Francisco Board of Supervisors (Development Agreement)
stageNote: The Planning Commission approved the office project in July 2019 and the Board of Supervisors passed its Development Agreement in January 2020. No building permit has been issued; the five site permit applications filed in 2019 are still pending. The developer has since applied to amend the Development Agreement and rezone the site for a revised project with up to 3,532 homes, which is under environmental review. Planning's 2026 development pipeline data describe the former Flower Mart buildings as vacant.

timeline.event: SF Planning opens case 2017-000663 for the redevelopment of the Flower Mart site.
Planning Commission certifies the Central SoMa Plan EIR (Motion 20182); the plan names the Flower Mart a key development site.
Planning Commission holds an informational hearing on the project.
Planning Department finds the project covered by the Central SoMa Plan EIR (community plan evaluation).

Planning Commission approves the project: Large Project Authorization (Motion 20484) and office allocation for its first phase (Motion 20485), and recommends the code and zoning changes (Resolution 20483) and the Development Agreement (Resolution 20486).
Site permit applications for the garage and four buildings are filed with DBI; none has been issued.
Board of Supervisors passes the Development Agreement with KR Flower Mart, LLC (Board File 190682) and the related code changes (Board File 190681) on second reading.
The developer files a revised project (record 2025-008569) with office/lab, residential, mixed-use and institutional scenarios; its environmental review opens on Sept 24, 2025.
Applications to amend the Development Agreement, the Planning Code and the Zoning Map are filed.

Planning Commission holds an informational hearing on the Development Agreement amendment: up to 3,532 homes, a new Flower Mart Special Use District, and height limits raised to between 350 and 600 ft.

nextMilestone: Environmental review of the revised project, then Planning Commission and Board of Supervisors hearings on the Development Agreement amendment, the rezoning and the Flower Mart Special Use District.
summary: A 6.5-acre site on Brannan Street between 5th and 6th streets, long home to the San Francisco Flower Mart. The City approved about 2 million sq ft of office and a new flower market here in 2019, but nothing was built; the developer now proposes to amend the deal for a mix that could include up to 3,532 homes, with height limits raised to between 350 and 600 ft.
